input.question: If 3-phase is more efficient, why isn't everything 3-phase?
input.ground_truth: 3-phase is only more efficient if you have a balanced 3-phase load. It does then require less conductor area than the same power delivered over single phase. But every piece of equipment would need to be 3 phase to achieve this. For large industrial equipment it is worth investing in this, but it is not economic to do for lots of small pieces that can work equally well on single phase. You would save on the electrical distribution cost, but at the small scale the increased costs of connections, switches and controls would outweigh the saving in copper. Large office buildings tend to have three phase up to the distribution boards, but then use single phase to the sockets and appliances. There would also be higher voltage at the sockets, which would be a safety issue. The three phase is at 400v in UK, while single phase is 220, from the same supply, so more power is delivered for the same current in the 3 phase section, but at a lower, safer voltage in the single phase section.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: If 3-phase is more efficient, why isn't everything 3-phase?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine you have three friends helping you carry buckets of water. If all three friends carry water at the same time and work together smoothly, you get a lot of water very quickly. That's like 3-phase electricity—it helps send electricity more smoothly and with less waste, so it's more efficient.

But not everything needs three friends to help. Sometimes, you only need one friend to carry a small cup of water. That's like single-phase electricity—it's simpler and enough for small things, like lights in your home or your phone charger.

Also, using 3-phase electricity needs special wires and equipment, which can be more expensive and complicated for small things. So, we use 3-phase for big things like factories and big machines, but for little things, we use single-phase because it's easier and cheaper.

So, even though 3-phase is better at carrying a lot of electricity at once, not everything needs that much help!
